content:
As WhatsApp prepares to officially launch its username feature, users can now store a contact's username along with their name and phone number when adding a new contact. Here are the details.

The username field when adding a new contact has started rolling out to some WhatsApp users

Although usernames are already a common feature on most messaging platforms, WhatsApp has only recently begun to move away from its long-standing practice of identifying users solely by phone number.

WhatsApp began rolling out a username reservation mechanism earlier this year, allowing users to register their preferred username ahead of the feature's official launch to prevent identity impersonation by scammers.

Several weeks ago, WhatsApp began enabling the username feature for some iPhone users.

Now, according to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp has begun supporting a username field when users add a new contact. The field appears between the name field and the phone number field.

WABetaInfo reports:

WABetaInfo noted that the username field appears to be rolling out simultaneously to some users on both the WhatsApp Beta and the stable version.

When the author tested with the latest stable version, although the field was displayed, the system still showed a "this username is not on WhatsApp" message even when the entered username actually existed.

That said, this is yet another step forward for WhatsApp in catching up with its competitors, adding back a basic feature that many people felt should have been included long ago.
